notes: Cradle is the vertical arena: open metal walkways over a long drop, with almost no interior. It is the only stage where the map itself kills people regularly, which changes how every fight is fought.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: Falling off the structure is fatal, so the map contributes deaths on its own and knockback, panic movement and blind strafing are all far more dangerous here than elsewhere.
Driving an opponent toward an edge is a legitimate way to kill them, so positioning is aimed at where they will retreat to rather than only at where they are.
The open ironwork means opponents on other levels are visible and shootable without being reachable, so many engagements happen across the structure rather than along it.
Movement between levels runs through a small number of connections, and those are where the map can actually be controlled, since nothing else on it is enclosed.
nuance.because: The arena carries only five Door records across one hundred and fifty-two pads.

nuance.claim: With so few ways between levels, mines on the connecting walkways cover most vertical movement on the stage.
Explosives are unusually strong here because a near miss can put someone over an edge, so they do not need to be lethal to score.
The stage is compact and almost entirely open, so there is nowhere to reload or recover unobserved and contacts are frequent.
nuance.because: One hundred and fifty-two pads makes this the second smallest arena after Caves.

nuance.claim: A high spawn count on a small structure means opponents return to the fight almost immediately, so killing someone buys very little time.
nuance.because: Eight Spawn records across one hundred and fifty-two pads, one of the highest spawn densities of any stage.

nuance.claim: The open framework hides nobody, so ambushes are impossible and every fight is entered knowingly by both sides.
With one-hit kills and lethal drops, the safest place is against the inside of the structure rather than on the outer walkways, whatever the sightlines suggest.
An unarmed carrier is visible from everywhere and can be knocked off the structure, so holds are short and largely a matter of staying central.
